headline: Nifty looks set to open lower, near 22,600, because oil rose back above $115 overnight. The test today is whether it can get back above 22,700.

mood.label: Negative
mood.why: The bias score is −27 (mildly bearish), but only 2 of 4 checks agree. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: GIFT Nifty was near **22,613** at 08:33 IST, about 0.6% below Tuesday's close of 22,750.
Brent crude rose **1.3%** overnight to $115 after missile claims against a Saudi refinery. India imports most of its oil.
FIIs bought **₹4,240 crore** of shares on Tuesday. They have still sold ₹34,505 crore this month.
My call: a **weak start, then sideways trade**. Tuesday was flat, so there's no big move to bounce from. Confidence is low.
The US Fed decides at **23:30 IST**. No change is expected, but a December rate rise looks likely.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Global stocks rose, but oil climbed and India-linked signals were weak. That points to a lower open after a flat Tuesday.

points.text: US stocks rose: the S&P 500 gained 0.6% and the Nasdaq **1.2%**, led by chip stocks. Japan is up about 1.3% and Korea about 6% this morning.
Brent crude is up **1.3%** at $115.4, close to its highest level in a year. That's bad for the rupee, for inflation, and for oil, paint and airline companies.
Indian shares listed in the US fell: Infosys **−2.6%**, Wipro −2.4%, HDFC Bank −1.6%. That's a weak sign for IT and banks. I couldn't confirm why they fell.
The US 10-year bond rate is a little higher at **5.02%**, and the dollar is firmer. Higher US rates can pull foreign money away from India.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: I expect a lower open and then sideways trade, with low confidence.

points.text: Against Nifty: higher oil, GIFT Nifty about **136 points** lower, weak US-listed Indian shares, and a weak trend.
For Nifty: big FII buying, rising US and Asian stocks, and option sellers moving their main support up to **22,700** from 22,500.
An open near 22,613 would start **below** that support. If Nifty can't get back above it, 22,500 is the next level. A move back above 22,800, or oil below $113, would prove me wrong.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is down, but option sellers are building support. Overall the dashboard reads mildly bearish.

points.text: Nifty (22,750) is below its 50-day and 200-day averages (**24,084**), and its recent peaks and lows keep getting lower. Trend score: −1.33.

Open futures positions rose **11%** while the price was flat, which the dashboard reads as new bets on a fall (−1.75). But Tuesday was the monthly expiry, so this may just be positions moving to the next month.
Option sellers made many bets that Nifty stays above levels from 22,200 to 22,700 (score **+0.95**). The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) is steady at 1.06.
India VIX (the fear gauge) is **16.5** and rising, higher than on 76% of days in the last year. Expect bigger swings.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: FIIs bought heavily for one day, but their bigger bets still point to a fall.

points.text: FIIs bought a net **₹4,240 crore** on Tuesday after selling on Monday. That is a big day by the dashboard's rule.
Domestic funds sold ₹1,250 crore, which is unusual, but they have bought **₹45,246 crore** this month.
Only **11.7%** of FII index-futures positions are bets on a rise, and they added protection against a fall. A rush to close these bets could lift Nifty, but it hasn't started.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: The dashboard's world check reads Headwinds, mainly because of oil and the strong dollar.

points.text: Brent is up **30%** in three months, because of tension around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.
The dollar is near its highest level in a year, and the rupee is weak at **₹95.1** per dollar.
US bill rates show markets expect a Fed rate rise. Reports put the chance of one in December at about **75%**.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Mixed: strong at L&T and Bajaj Auto, weak profits at Maruti and Cipla.

points.text: L&T's profit rose about **27–33%** (the figure depends on how it's measured). Bajaj Auto's profit rose about 60%.
Maruti's sales rose 26%, but its profit fell **26%** on higher costs. Cipla's profit fell 37%.
I couldn't confirm analysts' forecasts. HUL reports today, and Jio Platforms lists after its **$3.1 billion** share sale.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: The Fed tonight, then other central banks and Reliance's results.

points.text: If the Fed hints at a **December rate rise** tonight, the dollar could get stronger and FIIs could keep selling.
Thursday: US growth and inflation data, and the European Central Bank's decision. Friday: the Bank of Japan's decision and **Reliance** results.
The next weekly options expiry is **3 November**. India's inflation data comes on 12 November.

levels.note: A close above 23,000 would point to a recovery. A close below 22,700 would bring 22,500 into view.

watch.text: Does Nifty open below **22,700**, and can it climb back?
Jio Platforms listing. A weak debut could weigh on Reliance.
US Fed decision and what it says about December.

bottom_line: Nifty is likely to open lower because oil rose back above $115 and the India-linked signals overnight were weak, even though US and Asian stocks rose. The dashboard leans mildly bearish (−27), but only 2 of 4 checks agree, so confidence is low. FII buying and new support at 22,700 are why the picture isn't worse. The main risk to this read is oil falling or a calm Fed, which could bring buyers back quickly.
